Arabic Five Pointed Star Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Arabic Five Pointed Star because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+066D, which you can use as ٭ in HTML, \066D in CSS, or type with Alt+1645 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Arabic Five Pointed Star is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+066D is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Arabic Five Pointed Star has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ٭ or the hex escape ٭.

How to type arabic five pointed star on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 1 6 4 5 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 1645.
  4. Release Alt. The Arabic Five Pointed Star character (٭) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type arabic five pointed star on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Arabic Five Pointed Star. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Arabic Five Pointed Star" and click the character to insert it.

How to use arabic five pointed star in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\066D"; ()
  • Python: \u066D or chr(0x66D)
  • JavaScript: \u066D or String.fromCodePoint(0x66D)
  • JSON: "\u066D"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ٭?

No legacy Alt code exists for Arabic Five Pointed Star because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+066D in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ٭ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ٭, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+1645 not work?

Alt+1645 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Arabic Five Pointed Star?

The Unicode codepoint for Arabic Five Pointed Star is U+066D. You can use this value in HTML as ٭, in CSS as \066D, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ٭ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+066D, then click it.
